Essential shortage becomes 0.000 kWh; minimum battery is 1.224 kWh; original flexible work unfinished is 0.000 kWh. Electrical feasibility only; no clinical safety or availability guarantee.
recovery.next_action: Review the proposed equipment times with staff. An energy technician must verify any hypothetical capacity or output change; this comparison does not authorize purchases or equipment control.
assumptions: Each option uses the same weather snapshot, essential equipment, efficiencies, absolute initial stored kWh and reserve target.
Only explicitly listed capacity, output or optional-work changes differ. More battery capacity begins with the same stored energy, not a full charge.
Solar and storage/output candidates are bounded sensitivity sizes, not real products; unchanged charge limits may still constrain them.
Rank: essential shortage, reserve shortfall and breaches, original flexible work unfinished, then normalized modeled change. This is not a cost ranking.
Normalized change sums fractional capacity increases and changed/postponed work divided by original flexible energy (denominators at least 1).
Smallest means smallest among tested candidates under this score, not a global minimum or a hardware sizing recommendation.
limitations: This evaluates energy feasibility under stated assumptions, not whether clinical operations are safe. No electricity guarantee or equipment control.
The starting battery is the operator’s assumed stored energy at local midnight. Tomorrow’s charge is not predicted by carrying today’s simulation forward.
Today is a complete local calendar-day scenario, including elapsed hours; this is not a real-time remaining-day controller.
PV energy = rated kW × hourly horizontal irradiation (kWh/m²) ÷ 1 kW/m² × existing performance ratio. Tilt, shading, temperature and inverter clipping are omitted.
Reduced-sunshine cases are user-chosen sensitivity tests, not confidence intervals or calibrated forecast probabilities. Each case is independently reoptimized.
Essential equipment hours and requirements stay fixed. Flexible energy is divisible and interruptible; medical appliance cycles and staffing constraints require separate validation.
No grid, generator, sub-hour starting surge, degradation, or multi-day reliability model is included.
Only individual interventions are tested; combinations, site installation feasibility, staffing, clinical acceptability and costs require human review.
Postponed optional work remains reported against the original workload; it is not counted as completed or as a full-work success.
Backup values are unmet delivered electrical kWh per hourly slot, not generator ratings, fuel quantities or purchase recommendations.
Numerical weather-model forecast, not a ground observation or measured clinic electricity generation.
Today includes elapsed hours from the current forecast series; it is not a now-to-midnight simulation.
